answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so an identity gains influence only through reachable, supported paths. A sybil cluster may label its nodes ocean, summit, or fable, but labels do not create edges: if its sparse external cut has low conductance, few walks enter it from honest nodes. Under a fixed starting distribution and bounded degree, min-cut and conductance bounds therefore limit the cluster’s reachable trust and aggregate voting weight, rather than letting fabricated identities multiply influence unchecked.
